resources.string: FileShare: notices when you tap \"Copy\" and sends what was copied to your Mac. It does not read the screen content.
Clipboard and files between this tablet and your Mac
Pair once with the QR code on your Mac
1. Install FileShare on your Mac (github.com/MarcoFilho1/fileshare).\n2. On the Mac, click ⇄ in the menu bar → Pair tablet….\n3. Point this tablet\'s camera at the QR code and tap the link.
Looking for the Mac on Wi-Fi…
End-to-end encrypted, only on your Wi-Fi
You\'ll see files arriving from the Mac
Needed to show files received from the Mac
Stays connected while the tablet sleeps
Recommended so the tablet doesn\'t drop the connection
Add it to Quick Settings to send with one tap
Copy text or an image on one device and paste it on the other.
In any app, tap Share → Send to Mac. They arrive in Downloads › FileShare on the Mac.
Drag files to ⇄ on the Mac. They arrive in Download › FileShare.
To connect again, you\'ll need to scan a new QR code on the Mac.
No app to open the folder
The tablet connects to the Mac on its own over Wi-Fi, encrypted. You can close this screen.
Scan the QR code again: on the Mac, click ⇄ → Pair tablet….
When you tap Copy in any app, FileShare sends what you copied to your Mac. Without this permission, use the Send to Mac button instead.

• Android only tells an app that you tapped Copy through an accessibility service.
• FileShare only gets the name of the button you tap and system notices (like "Copied"), just to recognize a copy.
• It can't read what's on the screen or what you type, and none of this leaves the tablet. Only what you copied goes to your Mac, encrypted, over your Wi-Fi.
• Everything else works without it: Mac → tablet, files and the Send to Mac button.
Copies made on the tablet will stop going to the Mac automatically. You can turn it back on here anytime.

In Accessibility settings:

1. Open Installed apps (or Downloaded apps).
2. Tap FileShare: automatic copy.
3. Turn it on and confirm.

Then come back here: you'll see a ✓.
